content: Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. The information provided here was last updated in May 2024. Important Note on Usage of This Information: This document serves as a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this product and your individual health needs. How to Use: Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically once daily. If you experience stomach upset, nausea, or vomiting, take the medication with meals. Discuss with your doctor whether dividing the daily dose into smaller doses taken multiple times a day may be beneficial. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking this medication, along with other tuberculosis (TB) medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve. Your doctor may also recommend taking vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) to prevent certain side effects, such as nerve problems, associated with ethionamide. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, increased saliva production, a metallic taste in the mouth, loss of appetite, or mouth sores. While many individuals tolerate this medication well, some may experience serious side effects. Your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before taking ethionamide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase the risk of liver disease or mental/mood changes. Ethionamide may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. If you have diabetes, this medication may lower your blood sugar levels. Regularly monitor your blood sugar as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of low blood sugar, such as sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in your hands or feet. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as ethionamide may harm an unborn baby. Avoid becoming pregnant while using this medication. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab Tests and Monitoring: While taking this medication, you may need regular lab and medical tests, such as sputum tests, eye/vision exams, liver and thyroid function tests, blood glucose levels, and complete blood counts. Missed Dose: It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Additional Information: This information is provided for general educational purposes and may not reflect the most current formulary details. Contact your healthcare provider or plan provider for the latest information. Always consult your healthcare professional for personalized advice regarding your health and medications.
